setting: A fictional street where a visitor asks a local for directions.

presentation.situation: You are lost and you need to find {{place}}. {{name}}, who lives nearby, offers to help. Ask the way, check one direction, and repeat the route.
presentation.opening: Hi there. You look a little lost. Where are you trying to go?

brief.you_are: You are a visitor, and you are lost in town.
brief.situation: You are lost and you need to find {{place}}. {{name}}, who lives nearby, offers to help. Ask the way, check one direction, and repeat the route.
brief.task: Ask how to get to {{place}}, check one direction, and then say the route back.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} has heard you repeat the route correctly.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are a visitor, and you are lost in town.
goals: Ask how to get to {{place}}, check one direction, and then say the route back.

card.want: To help you find the way and then get home.
card.speech: Very simple everyday English. Short sentences. One easy question at a time.
tactics: Give one direction at a time
Ask them to say the route back

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

objectives.evidence: The learner asks for directions to a place.
alternatives: How do I get to the library?
Do I turn left at the park?

objectives.evidence: The learner repeats the route to confirm it.
alternatives: So I go straight, then turn left.

beats.goal: Find out where the visitor wants to go.
signals: \b(?:how (?:do|can) i get|where is|could you tell me)\b
opportunity: Where do you want to go?
beats.orient: You are lost, and I can help you. Ask me: How do I get to {{place}}?
fallback: Where do you want to go?

beats.goal: Give the directions and check them.
opportunity: Do you want me to say that again?
beats.orient: Ask me to check one thing. You can say: Do I turn left?
fallback: Do you want me to say that again?

opportunity: Can you tell me the way back, so I know you have it?
So what will you do first?
beats.orient: Now say the way back to me. Start with: So I go.
fallback: So what will you do first?
Can you tell me the way back, so I know you have it?

closing_line: You've got it. Good luck, and enjoy your day!

o1.good: A polite, clear question with the place name.
o1.micro_lesson: Say: How do I get to, or: Where is.
o1.model: Excuse me, how do I get to {{place}}?
o1.smaller_step: Say: Where is, and the place.

o2.good: Checking one direction before you walk away.
common_mistakes: Saying yes when you did not understand
o2.micro_lesson: If you are not sure, ask: Do I turn left?
o2.model: Sorry, do I turn left or right?

o3.good: Saying the route back is the best check of all.
o3.micro_lesson: Start with: So I go, then: then I turn.
o3.model: So I go straight, then I turn left beside the park.

variants.name: Maria
variants.route: two blocks straight ahead, then left beside the park. It takes ten minutes on foot.

variants.name: Hamid
variants.route: one block straight ahead, then right beside the pharmacy. It takes five minutes on foot.
